quotes.quote: Africa: Ogowe, Congo, Quanza, Luculla, Chiloango.

sections.html:
• Scientific name: Parailia occidentalis (Pellegrin, 1901)
  • Common name: Dusky Glass Catfish
  • Type locality: Cape Lopez, Gabon.
  • Synonyms: Ailia occidentalis, Physailia ansorgii, Physailia occidentalis, Physailia villiersi
  • Etymology: The generic name comes from the Latin prefix par-, meaning equal, and Ailia, a genus of schilbeid catfishes, in reference to the similarity between this genus and Ailia.
  • Size: 85 mm (3.3 in) SL.
  • Identification: All species of this genus have no dorsal fin and are small, being no larger than 150 mm SL.
  • IUCN Red List: Least Concern (last assessed 2009).
Family: Schilbeidae. Size: 7 cm. Temperature: 23–26°C. pH: 6.5–7.2. Oviparous; eggs are unguarded.

Africa: Ogowe, Congo, Quanza, Luculla and Chiloango Rivers. Type locality: Cap Lopez, French Congo. The specific name occidentalis is Latin for western, referring to Cap Lopez, Gabon, on the west coast of Africa.

Confined to large and moderate rivers; sometimes penetrates into estuaries. A gregarious schooling species; such schools are probably an important prey for several larger carnivorous species. As well as living in the rivers, this species may venture into the brackish waters of estuaries.
As with all Parailia, it has four pairs of barbels and likes to be kept in a group in the aquarium.
Breeding: Unreported. There is no breeding report.

Description: dorsal spines 0; dorsal soft rays 0; anal spines 0; anal soft rays 51–68. Adipose fin present; inner side of the pectoral spine feebly serrated, with small to very small serrations; vomerine teeth usually absent. Colouration: the defining character of this species is a dark spot at the caudal peduncle and a dark band running from the head to the caudal peduncle.

IUCN Red List: Least Concern, as the species has a wide distribution with no known major widespread threats. Also assessed regionally as Least Concern for central Africa. Data within southern Africa are scarce and more comprehensive surveys are required; it is assessed as Data Deficient within this region.
